sentences.text:
THIS APPEAL COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY, JUDGMENT WAS DELIVERED THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MRS. JUSTICE P. SREE SUDHA  ORAL JUDGMENT 1.

This appeal is filed by the claimant against the judgment and award dated 26.09.2023 passed by the Senior Civil Judge and M.A.C.T. Jewargi, [for short 'Tribunal'] in MVC No.334/2021 seeking enhancement of compensation.
2. The injured claimant aged 42 years, met with an accident on 17.12.2020 and sustained grievous injuries.
Hence, she filed a claim petition before the NC: 2025:KHC-K:6794 HC-KAR Tribunal seeking compensation of Rs.13,60,000/-.

The Tribunal after considering the entire evidence on record, awarded the compensation of Rs.3,27,226/- with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till realization and directed respondent No.2 - Insurance Company to pay the compensation.
Aggrieved by the said award, the appellant-claimant has preferred this appeal.

3. Heard arguments of both the parties and perused the materials available on record.
4.
The main contention of the appellant is that the Tribunal has awarded inadequate compensation under all heads.
It is stated by the learned counsel for the claimant that the claimant has sustained grievous traumatic brain injury and had post head injury.
In support of the case, claimant examined the Doctor as PW2, who assessed 40% disability to the whole body, but the Tribunal has taken only 13.33%.

It is also contended that the claimant was earning Rs.20,000/- per month by household supervision work, but the Tribunal has taken the income as Rs.9,210/-
Eramma vs Chetan And Anr on 5 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/91010135/
2 NC: 2025:KHC-K:6794 HC-KAR per month and thus, the compensation awarded for loss of future earning capacity is on the lower side.
Therefore, requested to enhance the compensation.
5. It is submitted by the learned counsel for respondent No.2 - Insurance Company that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and proper and needs no interference.
6. Admittedly, it is case of the disability suffered by the claimant.
PW2 - Doctor, after clinical and radiological examination of the claimant, has issued Ex.P8 - Disability Certificate assessing 40% disability to the whole body.

7. Learned counsel for the claimant contended that the claimant sustained hemorrhagic contusion in L - F & T region, SAH in L - parietal region and diffuses cerebral edema and she was treated conservatively and discharged on 21.12.2020 in stable condition with advice to take antiseptic drugs for long time.

He also contended that NC: 2025:KHC-K:6794 HC-KAR PW2 has assessed 40%
disability to the whole body, but the Tribunal has taken only 1/3rd of 40% i.e., 13.33% which needs to be enhanced to 15%.

In reply, learned counsel for respondent No.2 - Insurance Company submits that the Doctor is not a Nero Surgeon, he is only Orthopaedic Surgeon, therefore, his assessment with regard to neurological condition cannot be relied upon.
Considering the nature of injuries and the evidence of PW2, this Court finds no reason to interfere with the disability assessed by the Doctor and taken by the Tribunal at 13.33%.
8. Though, the claimant states that she was earning Rs.20,000/- per month, she has not produced any document to prove the same.

As the accident is of the year 17.12.2020, as per the guidelines issued by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, this Court deems it appropriate to reassess the income of the claimant at Rs.13,750/- per month.

Accordingly, the claimant is entitled for loss of future earning as under:
NC: 2025:KHC-K:6794 HC-KAR Rs.13,750/- x 12 x 14 x 13.33% = Rs.3,07,923/-
9.
The claimant was admitted in the hospital for 5 days.

Considering the period of hospitalization,
nature of injuries and other relevant factors, this Court finds it reasonable to award an amount of Rs.75,000/- for pain and suffering, Rs.25,000/- for loss of amenities and Rs.30,000/- for transportation, extra nourishment and attendant charges.

Further, due to injuries the claimant might not have attended any work atleast for a period of 4 months, hence, this Court finds it reasonable to award Rs.55,000/- for loss of income during laid up period.
However, the compensation of Rs.88,974/- awarded by the Tribunal for medical expenses, needs no interference.

10. The compensation awarded by the Tribunal is modified as under:
Sl. Heads Award by the Award by this No. Tribunal Court 1 Pain and Rs.10,000/-
Rs.75,000/-
suffering NC: 2025:KHC-K:6794 HC-KAR 2 Medical Rs.88,974/- Rs.88,974/-

There will be enhancement of Rs.2,54,671/-
11.

In the result, the following order is passed:
 (i) Appeal is allowed in part.
(ii) The claimant is entitled for the enhanced compensation of Rs.2,54,671/- with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realization.
NC: 2025:KHC-K:6794 HC-KAR (iii) Respondent No.2 - Insurance Company is directed to deposit the entire compensation amount along with interest within one month from the date of this judgment.
(iv) On such deposit, the claimant is permitted to withdraw the entire amount along with interest accrued on it.
